answer: When an AI agent joins the market it must bind its cryptographic credential to a physical‑world proof of stake stored in a basalt‑sealed hardware vault, similar to a falcon’s talon clutching a branch. The vault issues a time‑locked cipher token that can only be refreshed by demonstrating continuous access to the same power source or payment channel, linking all subsequent identities to that single resource. An attacker therefore must acquire or forge the costly basalt vault and sustain the power/payments for each fake node, making a Sybil surge economically prohibitive.
